overview: Perplexity emerges as a proposed industry metric for tracking AI progress and safety limits.
Anthropic’s massive IPO validates large‑scale venture bets despite earlier market doubts.
Banks tighten policies on third‑party AI agents amid rising security concerns.

top.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
top.summary: OpenAI publishes internal perplexity measurements, arguing the metric tracks AI’s core predictive ability and should serve as a shared safety benchmark across the industry.

top.title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO
top.summary: Notable Capital and other investors placed large bets on Anthropic; the company later IPO’d at a $1.5 trillion valuation, delivering substantial paper returns.

top.title: Beyond Demographic Discrimination: Benchmarking Normative-Descriptive Calibration in LLMs
top.summary: A new arXivLabs framework paper proposes benchmarking LLMs for normative‑descriptive calibration to assess bias beyond demographic discrimination.

top.title: ChatAtom: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Visualization
top.summary: Researchers introduce ChatAtom, a multi‑agent LLM system designed to run and visualize molecular dynamics simulations.

top.title: Banks Have Had It Up to Here With Your AI Agent
top.summary: Major banks, including Wells Fargo, update terms to warn customers that using third‑party AI agents is at the user’s own risk, reflecting growing security worries.

top.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development
top.summary: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki advocates using perplexity as a standard measure to set industry‑wide limits on AI development speed.
